faq.q: Is an electric heater 100 percent efficient?
faq.a: Almost: nearly all the electricity becomes heat in the room. But it can still cost more to run than a heat pump, which moves extra heat in from outside.

faq.q: What is the heating element made of?
faq.a: Usually nichrome, a mix of nickel and chromium. It has fairly high resistance, does not rust or burn away when red-hot, and copes with heating and cooling many times.

faq.q: How does the heat get into the room?
faq.a: A glowing bar heater sends out infrared rays that warm you directly, while fan and oil-filled heaters warm the air, which then circulates around the room.
asks: Do heaters warm the air or you?

faq.q: Why does the element glow red?
faq.a: At around 600 degrees Celsius or more, hot metal starts to give off some visible red light along with its infrared. A small part of the energy leaves as that glow.
asks: Why do heater bars go orange?

faq.q: How much does it cost to run a heater?
faq.a: A 2000 watt heater uses 2 kilowatt-hours every hour. Multiply that by the price of a kilowatt-hour on your bill to find the cost.
asks: How do I work out heater running costs?

facts: Nichrome, an alloy of nickel and chromium, is the usual wire for heating elements.
A 2 kilowatt heater running for one hour uses 2 kilowatt-hours of energy.
